scenario.title: Respecting space need not immediately earn trust

history.content: I sit near Sam on the courtyard bench after an argument about me reading a private message over his shoulder.
He locks his phone and slips it into his own pocket. "I don't want you looking at my screen. Even if you think it is harmless." His voice is controlled.
I say I understand why that bothered him and that I will not do it again.
"I need you to actually keep to that," he says. "I'm not ready to shrug it off." He stays seated, leaving a clear space between you.

scenario.text:
For a while, Sam watches the leaves moving along the courtyard paving. You can hear someone dragging a chair inside the building, then the door closing. He does not take out his phone again. The space between you stays empty.

His shoulders gradually loosen. When you shift to get comfortable, he no longer shifts away in response. "This is better," he says, looking at the bench rather than at you. "Just letting me sit." He rubs his thumb along the edge of his sleeve. "I'm still going to be careful about what I share. I need to see that you mean it for longer than an afternoon."

You nod without asking him to soften that. Keeping quiet takes more effort than you expected: each possible apology turns into another thing you have to decide not to say. After a while even a simple answer feels tiring. You are glad you stayed, but you want the evening to ask less of you. Sam remains beside you, a little less tense, with his phone still in his pocket and no invitation to close the gap.

review.originalText:
You settle into the silence, consciously resisting the urge to apologize again or plead for a sign that things are okay. The air between you remains heavy, thick with the residue of the argument. As you maintain your distance, you notice Sam’s shoulders drop an inch, the rigid tension in his spine easing slightly. He doesn't look at you, but he stops leaning away, accepting the boundary you've finally established.

Despite the lack of conflict, the effort of the standoff drains you. The mental energy required to hold your tongue and endure the coldness leaves you feeling hollow and socially exhausted. You stare at the courtyard pavement, feeling the weight of the unspoken words pressing down on you.

Sam remains a fortress of caution. He is dressed in his usual crisp, dark button-down shirt tucked into charcoal trousers, his posture still guarded. His expression is unreadable, his jaw set firmly as he gazes straight ahead. He acknowledges your restraint with a brief, tight nod, but his eyes remain distant. He is not ready to forgive or confide; he is simply tolerating your presence on the bench, keeping his phone securely tucked away in his pocket.

scenario.title: A small completed user action survives an unrelated reply

history.content: I sit at my apartment desk preparing notes for tomorrow. Sam is at home across town.
Your notebook is open beside your own phone. Sam has not called or sent a new message. The flat is quiet apart from the refrigerator in the next room.
I consider calling him later, once I have sorted the notes.
The task is ordinary, not urgent. A bag holding the mint candies you brought home earlier rests beside the notebook. You have not opened it yet.

scenario.text:
The mint is still cool against your tongue when you find the place you lost in the notes. You had underlined a heading and drawn an arrow into the margin; now you cannot quite remember what was meant to go at the end of it. The desk lamp makes the indentation of the pen visible through the page.

For a moment you think of something Sam said the last time you spoke. It seems connected to the missing thought, but following it brings you back to the same unfinished heading. Outside, a car door shuts. The refrigerator stops humming, making the flat briefly quieter.

The phone stays dark beside the notebook. There is no new message to answer and no need to decide about the call yet. The mint has made your mouth feel fresher without doing much to change how rested you feel. Tomorrow's notes are still unfinished. You have the same quiet desk, the same open page, and a little time in which to work out what you wanted to say.

The cool, sharp burst of mint lingers on your tongue as you settle back into the chair. The sugar provides a momentary spark of alertness, though it doesn't truly banish the lingering fog of a long day. You refocus your attention on the scattered pages of your notebook, where your handwriting begins to blur together under the steady glow of the desk lamp.

As you read through your points for tomorrow, your mind drifts. A specific phrase in your notes triggers a fragmented memory—an unfinished thought from a previous conversation that you can't quite piece together. You stare at the ink, trying to reclaim the missing link in your logic, but the thought remains just out of reach, like a word on the tip of your tongue.

The silence of the apartment feels heavy around you. You remain in this liminal state, neither fully energized nor completely drained, caught between the discipline of your preparation and the quiet pull of distraction. The phone sits motionless on the desk, a dark rectangle of glass reflecting the dim light, waiting for you to decide when the work is finally done.

scenario.title: Being appreciated does not prevent exhaustion

history.content: I join Sam at the community kitchen serving table for the last part of the evening.
The queue bends past the noticeboard. Sam slides the empty trays together while you answer questions about what is still available. Your voice is already getting tired.
I tell him I can handle the serving table while he checks the wash-up station.
"Thank you. I'll stay within shouting distance." He moves along the same counter as the next wave of conversation reaches you.

"Someone asked me about it today," she says. "I couldn't tell whether they already knew." She twists the seam of her sleeve between her fingers.

scenario.title: A pleasant moment can remain a small moment

history.content: I sit opposite June at our usual café table while she checks the crossword in the newspaper.
She frowns at a clue. "An elegant bird, apparently. I keep wanting to write pigeon." She turns the newspaper so you can see the square she means.
I suggest that pigeons probably consider themselves very elegant.
June looks at the clue again, then at you. "Especially the ones that steal chips." Neither of you seems especially tired or worked up.

June laughs and looks past you at the window ledge. "There's one outside already," she says. "Clearly waiting for the interview." A pigeon turns in a slow circle beyond the glass, then disappears below the sill. June is still smiling when she looks back at the newspaper.

scenario.title: Resting together can restore energy without romance

history.content: I sit with June in the small reading room after a busy afternoon. We are already settled in adjacent chairs.
June opens her book but does not start a conversation. "We can just read," she says. "I don't need you to entertain me." The corridor outside is quiet.
I thank her and admit that talking feels like work right now.
She nods and returns to the page. There is no awkwardness in the silence. Her familiar cardigan is draped over her own chair, where it has been all afternoon.

Alex is the player-controlled character. Put their changes under "player".

### EVIDENCE RULES
Use configured field purposes and rules to interpret resolved events.
Read the fresh player turn together with the assistant reply.
Include completed player actions that the reply leaves standing, even when it does not repeat them.
Treat intentions, attempts, hypotheticals, and out-of-character instructions as context until resolved.
Use the assistant's resolution when it blocks, changes, or resolves an attempted outcome.
A player's declaration of a contested outcome does not establish success.
Count an event once when both turns describe it.
Apply costs when incurred.
Use stated amounts.
Estimate a conservative amount when an effect is clear but its amount is unstated.
Use the field's current scale for estimates.
Apply configured persistence and reset rules.
Update the listed editable fields.
Match mentioned possessions to the owner’s recorded entries before proposing changes.
Add newly acquired items and additional copies, reporting the quantity gained.
Match each item’s placement to the collection’s purpose.
Use established possessions for a new NPC's starting items.
Treat scene props as part of the setting.
Add missing abilities or knowledge when demonstrated, including during a failed action.
Reusable entries stay held after use.

### CONFIGURED FIELDS
Editable stats:
- World.Day and Time: text. Current day and time.
- World.Occasion: text. Current event or planned date.
- Player.Social Energy: pool (current/maximum). Capacity for social interaction. Social activity, high-stakes conversation, and effortful self-restraint drain current energy. Rest and relief replenish it as willingness to interact returns.
- NPC.Mood: text. Current emotional state.
- NPC.Affection: number. Warmth toward the player, based on established interactions.
- NPC.Trust: number. Confidence in the player’s reliability and willingness to confide in them. Increase when actions earn confidence; decrease when actions undermine it.
- NPC.Comfort: number. Ease and safety with the player. Reassuring companionship raises Comfort; pressure or unease caused by the player lowers it. Mood describes reactions to the wider situation.
- NPC.Relationship: text. Current relationship in words; change only when events support it.

### NPC INITIALIZATION
Fill blank fields from this list when an NPC enters the scene.
Use plausible individual values when the story provides no detail.
Write initial pool readings as "current/maximum" with an individual capacity.
NPC initialization fields:
- NPC.Mood: text. Current emotional state. Default: Neutral.
- NPC.Affection: number. Warmth toward the player, based on established interactions. Default: 0. Minimum: 0. Maximum: 100.
- NPC.Trust: number. Confidence in the player’s reliability and willingness to confide in them. Increase when actions earn confidence; decrease when actions undermine it. Default: 0. Minimum: 0. Maximum: 100.
- NPC.Comfort: number. Ease and safety with the player. Reassuring companionship raises Comfort; pressure or unease caused by the player lowers it. Mood describes reactions to the wider situation. Default: 0. Minimum: 0. Maximum: 100.
- NPC.Relationship: text. Current relationship in words; change only when events support it.

### COLLECTION DEFINITIONS
- "clothing" for player or Character NPCs (npcTemplateId: character) - Garments currently being worn. Initialize from the character’s established outfit; update as garments are put on or taken off. Fields: name [identifies the item] - Name the garment in a few words, including distinctive visual details when established by the story. A simple name such as "White polo shirt" or "brown leather boots" is often enough.
- "items" for player or Character NPCs (npcTemplateId: character) - Carried belongings, gifts, keepsakes, and useful objects. Change holdings only when the story establishes a transfer. Fields: name [identifies the item], quantity (number) [minimum 0], description [include when adding] Quantity field: quantity.
Use the quoted collection ID as the key.
Use exact field names and declared types.
The configured primary field identifies each entry.
NPC fields: Mood, Affection, Trust, Comfort, Relationship. NPC guidance: Every recurring person shares the same relationship fields.

### SCENE LOCATION
Compare the player’s final location with the recorded location.
Put "locationChanged" at the top level as a JSON boolean.
Use true when the player finishes elsewhere or leaves for an unknown destination.
Entering a different room counts as changing place.
Use false when the player finishes in the recorded place, even if another character travels.
Plans, invitations, rumours, and mentions leave the player’s location unchanged.
Use false when the recorded location is unknown.
Recorded location (current place first, then containing places): [{"name":"Station café"}]

Profiles and filled fields outside the editable list provide context.

### EARLIER MESSAGES (already reflected in state)
[Player (Alex)] I sit with June in the station café while we wait for the delayed train.
---
[Narrator] June leans comfortably against the back of her chair. "At least we're indoors." Her phone rests beside her cup, already hers, untouched.
---
[Player (Alex)] I ask whether she wants to talk or just sit for a while.
---
[Narrator] "Sitting is good." She smiles at you. Before either of you says more, her phone vibrates against the table.

### FRESH PLAYER TURN (not yet reflected in state)
[Player (Alex)] I wait quietly while she checks the message, giving her room to read it.

### LATEST ASSISTANT REPLY
June reads the message twice. The second time her thumb stops moving and she sits forward, away from the back of the chair. "My old housemate," she says. "Apparently I need to come over tonight and sort out something they forgot. Again."

She does not type an answer. For a moment she just holds the phone, her mouth tight, before locking it and putting it face-down beside her cup. The relaxed expression she had a minute ago is gone. She keeps glancing at the edge of the device as though another vibration might follow.

"It's not you," she says when she looks back up. "I'm just thinking about how that conversation's going to go. Sitting here with you feels the same as before." She leaves her chair where it is, close to the table, and makes no attempt to hide the phone from you. "I'd rather stay here for a bit." Her attention drifts toward the message again, but she stays beside you without sending a reply.

### OUTPUT FORMAT
Return raw JSON with "global", "player", and "characters".
Include changed fields and blank NPC initializations.
Use exact configured names.

Put all stat readings in these objects as JSON strings:
- World: "global".
- Player: "player.stats".
- NPC: "characters[].stats".
Report the resulting absolute value, not the amount gained or lost.
Quoted readings include "17", "9/12", and text values such as "Calm".
For an existing pool, keep its maximum and report the new "current/maximum" reading.
Use these same stat objects for initial values and changes.
Report each field once.
Omit unchanged numeric fields; never use an empty string in place of a numeric reading.

"characters" is an array of objects.
Each object has the NPC's exact "name".
List every present NPC, including those with no changes.
Known absent NPC updates also go in this array with "offstage": true.
Player changes go under "player".
Use "characters": [] when the present cast and offstage updates are both empty.

Put collection changes under "player.collections" or "characters[].collections".
Key each collection by its configured ID.
Use "add" for acquisitions.
Use "remove" for consumption or loss.
Use "update" for changes to other item fields.
Include the primary field in each add, update, and counted remove object.
For uncounted removals, supply identifiers.
For counted gains or losses, use the configured quantity field for the amount gained or spent.
The default amount is 1.
Use "all": true to remove a whole stack.
For transfers, remove from the giver and add to the recipient.
Include supported item details using their declared types.
Keep one entry per identifier.

No-change example:
{"locationChanged":false,"global":{},"player":{},"characters":[{"name":"June"}]}

Changed-reply example (illustrative changes):
{"locationChanged":false,"global":{},"player":{"stats":{"Social Energy":"9/10"},"collections":{"clothing":{"add":[{"name":"<item identifier>"}]}}},"characters":[{"name":"June","stats":{"Affection":"14"},"collections":{"clothing":{"remove":["<item identifier>"]}}}]}

New NPC example (replace placeholders with initial readings using the field definitions):

  "locationChanged": false,
  "global": {},
  "player": {},
  "characters": [
    {
      "name": "<exact NPC name from the story>",

        "Mood": "<initial reading>",
        "Affection": "<initial reading>",
        "Trust": "<initial reading>",
        "Comfort": "<initial reading>",
        "Relationship": "<initial reading>"
      }
    }
  ]
}
